subject.title: Feature: let an outbound hook override the reply threadId (reply into an auto-created forum topic, not only the inbound thread)

question: Should regular reply delivery expose a public plugin override for the destination thread, and if so should it be a dedicated typed delivery-target hook result rather than an extension of a content-oriented hook?
rationale: The choice establishes a public plugin contract and determines whether plugins may alter message routing, including the scope and validation needed to prevent unintended delivery.

options.title: Typed delivery override
options.body: Add a generic optional destination override constrained to the selected channel, account, and conversation, with Telegram interpreting its thread field as message_thread_id.

options.title: Telegram placement setting
options.body: Extend Telegram child-placement configuration to regular top-level replies, accepting a broader channel-specific policy surface rather than per-turn plugin control.

options.title: Keep routing immutable
options.body: Leave reply routing inbound-derived and require plugins to perform separate sends, preserving the current boundary but retaining duplicate and fidelity problems.

recommendation.title: Typed delivery override
recommendation.body: Add a generic optional destination override constrained to the selected channel, account, and conversation, with Telegram interpreting its thread field as message_thread_id.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision primarily changes the hook contract introduced by this person's related merged work, with Telegram-area review still needed for adapter semantics.
